parole.significato: Increasing the amount or frequency of urination.
parole.testo: From Middle English diuretyk, from Old French diuretique; ultimately from Ancient Greek διουρητικός (diourētikós). By surface analysis, diuresis + -etic.

parole.testo: From Middle English mytre, from Old French mitre, from Ancient Greek μίτρα (mítra, “headband, turban”). Its use in reference to a counterfeit coin derived from the bishop's mitre stamped upon it. Doublet of Mithras, Mithra, Mitra, and Mehr.

parole.significato: A hard igneous rock consisting of large crystals in a fine-grained matrix.
parole.testo: From Old French porfire, from Ancient Greek πορφυρίτης λίθος (porphurítēs líthos, “purple stone”), from πορφύρα (porphúra, “purple-fish, purple dye”).

parole.significato: A split or separation within a group or organization, typically caused by discord.
parole.testo: From Middle English scisme, from Old French cisme or scisme, from Ancient Greek σχίσμα (skhísma, “division”), from σχίζω (skhízō, “I split”). Doublet of schisma. Compare chasm. parole.significato: A heavy woven cloth, often with decorative pictorial designs, normally hung on walls.
parole.testo: From Middle English tapestrie, from Old French tapisserie (“tapestry”), from Ancient Greek τάπης (tápēs), from an Iranian source.

parole.significato: A silicate mineral of aluminium and fluorine, usually tinted by impurities.
parole.testo: From Old French topace (compare French topaze), from Ancient Greek τόπαζος (tópazos).
